localContext: Mount Prospect experiences harsh Chicago winters. Many homes, built in the 1950s and 60s, feature original steel garage doors. These often have single-skin, un-insulated panels. On subzero January days, these older doors visibly bow inward. This bowing causes tracks to bind. It also overworks the garage door opener and other components. Cables stretch and fray under this increased strain. In neighborhoods like We-Go Park and Downtown Mount Prospect, these conditions accelerate wear on lift cables and drums. Cold temperatures make the cables stiff. Years of use, combined with thermal stress, lead to premature cable failure. We understand these specific challenges for Mount Prospect garages.
